- "When using this permission, the backing application of the service principal being created must in the local tenant"
  - The issue is clear. When Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy tries to create a service principal, Graph requires the backing application to be "in the local tenant" — which it IS, but Graph is also returningAuthorization_RequestDenied when the SP already exists (instead of the expected ObjectConflict). This is likely a Graph API behavior difference depending on the permission level. The fix: also treat Authorization_RequestDenied with "backing application" message as an idempotent success (SP already exists), OR better — check if the SP exists before trying to create it:
  - Interesting — I can reproduce it with my own identity too. But the app IS in the local tenant... Let me check if the app registration has some unusual property"
  - "The "must in the local tenant" error message is misleading — it actually means "you don't have ownership of this app under Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy."
  - Root cause: The error was genuine Entra replication lag, not an ownership problem. The provisioner creates the app (becoming owner), then tries to create the SP 2 seconds later. Graph's SP directory hasn'treplicated the app yet, returns "backing application...must in the local tenant" with Authorization_RequestDenied code. Our _handle_auth_error then rewrites it to "Insufficient privileges" — completely misleading.
    What we fixed:
    1. _ensure_service_principal now retries this specific error (10×3s = 30s window) — already deployed
    2. _handle_auth_error now gives a clear "replication timeout, re-run" message if retries still exhaust — just committed
  - payne@papayne-issued:~/repos/community-search$ [@amplifier-online](project:9dd68fa2-8f12-47a3-9c7b-6b74c0bf9992) up
      Ensuring app registration...
      Error: [DEPLOYMENT_FAILED] [@Microsoft](organization:4ae25353-5ebb-4725-936a-84b5eb4684e4) Graph API error: InvalidValue: Property api.preAuthorizedApplications.delegatedPermissionIds has a Permission Id that cannot be found in the AppPermissions sets.
- Next: Remove knowledge of all but the ACA stack from the provisioner and focus on getting that working end-to-end.
- _if_ that still is flaky, remove stacks entirely and base this version of AO on ACA only. This will require rewrites by other team projects that don't use ACA. But the bundle should help there.

---

Here's what EasyAuth on the backend actually gives you:

 1. Token validation — rejects requests without a valid Bearer token (Return401)
 2. X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL header — injects decoded token claims (user ID, name, groups) into the request so the app doesn't need to decode JWTs itself
 3. allowedApplications — accepts tokens from both Azure CLI (az login) AND the app's own SPA (MSAL.js) without the backendneeding to know about either

And the group claims issue you recall: the token DOES contain groups (we configured groupMembershipClaims: "SecurityGroup" +optionalClaims), but EasyAuth's X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL header wasn't reliably forwarding the multi-valued groups array. That'swhy we added the JWT-decode fallback in the provisioner's middleware.

So yes — EasyAuth on the backend gives you almost everything for free:

 - CLI users authenticate via az login → token accepted ✓
 - SPA users authenticate via MSAL.js → token accepted ✓
 - Groups are in the token (for authorization decisions)
 - No secrets needed (public client validation only)

The only thing EasyAuth doesn't do is authorization (deciding what groups/roles can do what) — that's still app logic.

title: Journal/Notes Information Architecture for Wild Life
body:
## Analysis Findings on Current Note Structure
1. **Current Practice**: All notes are categorized solely as `journal` with no primary entity attachments. They use tags and links to organize content.
- Tags include: `work:microsoft`, `relationships`, `divorce`, `marriage`, with others for specific use cases (e.g., `whiteboard`).
- **Risk of Orphaned Notes**: Given the lack of entity attachments, notes could be easily lost, especially if reliance solely on tags occurs...

## PKM Tool Research Summary
1. **Notion**: Operates with topic-scoped pages and a functional search but may lead to over-organization risks. Focused on project management more than pure journaling alignment.
2. **Obsidian**: Built for atomic note management with networking via backlinks, strong for interlinked notes and discoverability but requires a deliberate structure to prevent orphaned notes.
3. **Roam Research**: Prioritizes direct linking of ideas, great for daily notes and journaling with atomic management in mind.
4. **Logseq**: Similar to Roam but more approachable for users needing structured data management and effective graph representations.
5. **Bullet Journal Method**: Focuses on daily logs, task flexibility, with significant for personal reflection without rigid scheduling.

## Proposed IA Options for Wild Life
- **(A)** **Unified Journal**: All notes as a single stream with cross-referencing via links and tags, allowing flexibility in content visualization.
- **(B)** **Per-Area Journals**: Separate journals for each Area, pulling together Program rollups to organize content effectively but increases the likelihood of duplicate notes.
- **(C)** **Per-Program Journals**: Require Program attachments for entries, ensuring relevance but risking disconnect for notes that don't fit neatly.

## Recommendation
Given the existing unified approach, I recommend Option A: a **Unified Journal** structure. This retains current simplicity while enhancing users' ease of finding notes, maintain discoverability, and encourages fluid cross-entity connections to avoid orphaning notes over time. Enhancements could include automated tagging suggestions or common link patterns based on frequent topics.

---

title: Reconnecting with childhood wonder
body:
Back in the days starting therapy, it felt like I was disconnected from
my childhood dreams... or from my childhood memories. I didn't know
what I liked or wanted. I felt aimless... especially after having lost
my faith... after having lost [@Jen](person:79ed28f0-e91e-42aa-99a2-3d50bbaab49c). I was confronted with [@Paul Chan](person:4249ed73-1a87-4393-9ab8-e7ab6111b46c)'s
success. I started to feel like I was left behind... like I failed at
life... like I didn't measure up.

At some point in trying to reconnect, I began to feel the wonder and
curiosity of being a child again. It is this that gave me motivation
again. Something in that feels open, undying... like possibilities are
opening up instead of grinding down.

Have I maintained this sense of possibility? Or am I grinding again? If
I had stayed at [@Navigating Cancer](organization:8460175c-2e5c-40c1-a982-a99588f83e76), I would definitely feel as though I
were grinding. I moved on and am on an upward trajectory again. It still
sometimes feels like a grind, though. Especially when the assignments
keep coming, the days at work start flowing one to another, and dreams
stay off in the distance... an artist, a meaningful
contribution.

Today I thought what I am really seeking is a meaningful contribution
that will make my fortune. That would be success. Maybe it is that
simple. The fortune is both the reward and the evidence of the
contribution's impact. This is perhaps why I disdain fortunes made over
meaninglessness; why I disdained [@Facebook](organization:ed30b3f0-4ddb-418a-8355-905695d85747), sales, marketing, hype,
stupid startups. But I honor the fortunes made by [@Google](organization:36688ebc-bac0-4b02-94df-5062562056e6) (let the
marketers spend their money on Adwords). I honor pioneers and
innovators. I honor artists. I honor the hard work that changes lives
and makes fortunes.

That is a taste of immortality... to the human race and to your
progeny.

My paths to this future are: health, AI, hardware design,
entrepreneurship, innovation ([@Nordstrom](organization:b5839411-ae0b-43fd-b329-865113fed870)), Google, artistic skill.
Perhaps a probability decision matrix or dependency graph would be
beneficial.

title: Meeting: Team meeting
body:
# Team Meeting Notes — 2026-06-25

## Strong candidates for packaging or spin-off

### 1. [@Amplifier](project:d5f8fb75-ba6d-4a26-9795-0b42c1a139fb) Agent

Discussed as a potentially useful out-of-the-box experience that could be used by other teams and even externally.

Key theme:

- Make Amplifier Agent usable outside the immediate Amplifier ecosystem.
- Potentially distribute it as a CLI experience.
- Could become a way to demonstrate best practices developed by the team.

### 2. [@Amplifier Online](project:9dd68fa2-8f12-47a3-9c7b-6b74c0bf9992) (AO)

Your area came up specifically.

[@Brian](person:6f790c53-9404-4b7e-86de-4498a071899d) explicitly said:

> "Paul's work on Amplifier Online ... would be a really, really good one."

The reasoning was:

- Valuable for teams that fit the team's operating model.
- After provisioning/setup, much of the experience becomes very simple.
- Could enable team-level AI workflows without requiring users to understand all of Amplifier internals.

### 3. Wiki Weaver

One of the clearest examples.

Brian described Wiki Weaver as:

- Already useful.
- Designed originally for Team Pulse needs.
- Useful independently for:
  - transcripts
  - document collections
  - personal knowledge
  - other content repositories

The discussion repeatedly returned to Wiki Weaver as an example of a reusable, standalone capability.

### 4. Repo Weaver

Presented as the companion to Wiki Weaver.

Purpose:

- More focused on repositories/codebases.
- Built using the same packaging pattern.
- Can run in multiple environments.
- Described as another example of something that could be reused outside the team.

### 5. PR Reviewer That Learns (Samuel's self-improving PR review system)

A significant portion of the meeting focused on this.

Core concept:

- Review PRs.
- Continuously improve its own review rubric.
- Use escaped defects/fixes as learning signals.
- Human remains in the loop via approval of rubric updates.

Brian and others repeatedly referenced this as an example of something potentially valuable beyond the team.

### 6. GitHub Issues / PR Automation Work

[@Salil](person:80352a40-7fd6-4037-902a-497ec4015e71)'s list included:

> "the issues and PR work"

and Mark's PR tooling was also discussed.

Examples included:

- PR responder
- PR review automation
- Issue triage
- Self-improving review processes

These were repeatedly referenced as packaging candidates.

### 7. Eval-Driven Development

Salil explicitly added:

> "the evals work"

The idea:

- Packaging parts of the team's evaluation-based development methodology.
- Possibly sharing the tooling, patterns, or workflows rather than just internal usage.

### 8. Team-level AI Infrastructure Patterns

The team discussed making available:

- Team provisioning approaches
- Team AI operating environment patterns
- Infrastructure that enables team-centered AI workflows

This was largely discussed in connection with AO.

## Mentioned as potentially interesting, but not yet mature

### 9. Context Intelligence

Salil specifically raised Context Intelligence as another possibility.

The group's reaction was essentially:

- Valuable internally.
- Producing lots of leverage.
- Not yet at the "half-day to package and release" stage.
- Probably requires additional work before becoming a spin-off offering.

So it was discussed, but not accepted as an immediate candidate.

## Explicitly called out as not good candidates right now

These were important because Brian used them as examples of things that would snowball into major products.

### 10. Amplifier Stories

The team specifically decided not to package this now.

Reason:

- Would quickly grow into:
  - stories
  - infographics
  - PowerPoints
  - many adjacent features

Brian explicitly cited it as an example where they needed discipline and should say "not now."

### 11. Attractor Pipeline UX/Productization

Salil identified:

> "the attractor pipeline"

as another example that could easily explode in scope.

The team agreed:

- Valuable.
- Interesting.
- Not something they wanted to spin off right now because of UX, productization, and supporting work required.

## The closest thing to the final consolidated list

Salil actually summarized the candidate set during the meeting:

> "the Amplifier Agent pipelines, Wiki Weaver, Ken's issues/PR work, Samuel's PR review additions, Amplifier Online, the evals work"

and then added:

> "Context Intelligence itself, if it can be packaged differently"

with the caveat that Context Intelligence was probably not ready.

So the effective shortlist coming out of the discussion was:

- Amplifier Agent
- Amplifier Online (AO)
- Wiki Weaver
- Repo Weaver
- Issues/PR automation tooling
- Self-learning PR Reviewer
- Eval-driven development / eval tooling
- Context Intelligence (exploratory, not ready)

And the explicit "not now" list was:

- Amplifier Stories
- Attractor Pipeline productization / UX experience

---

## Workflows discussed

### 1. Evaluation-Driven Development (Brian's primary workflow)

This was probably the most strongly advocated workflow in the meeting.

Process:

- Start with the goal/outcome.
- Enter evaluation mode immediately.
- Let the system build test/evaluation harnesses.
- Use Council/RB-style review to critique designs.
- Implement and evaluate repeatedly.
- Compare alternatives quantitatively.
- Choose the best result.

The important nuance is that Brian is trying to spend less effort specifying implementation details and more effort defining:

- desired outcomes
- acceptance criteria
- constraints
- success measures

The AI does much of the design and implementation exploration.

### 2. Parallel Exploration / Evolutionary Search

Brian described doing multiple competing explorations simultaneously.

Example pattern:

```
Problem
  ↓
Approach A
Approach B
Approach C
  ↓
Run evaluations
  ↓
Compare outcomes
  ↓
Keep winner
```

He described using this for:

- Wiki Weaver
- Team Pulse components
- M365 Pull exploration
- Attractor pipeline work

Rather than debating designs up front, the workflow is:

> Build several candidates, evaluate them, select the winner.

### 3. Long-Running Session Development

A number of people discussed very long-lived sessions.

Brian mentioned:

- thousands of turns
- single sessions spanning substantial projects

The philosophy is:

```
Project
  ↓
Persistent session
  ↓
Accumulating context
  ↓
Incremental evolution
```

Instead of recreating context every day.

This triggered substantial discussion because others were wondering whether long-running sessions degrade quality.

### 4. Workspace-as-Project-Memory

Multiple people independently converged on this.

The workflow:

```
Workspace
  ├── designs
  ├── plans
  ├── scratch artifacts
  ├── generated documents
  └── instructions
```

The key idea is:

> Context lives in files, not in the session.

Diego was particularly explicit about this.

Rather than relying on chat history:

- design docs are stored
- agent-generated reasoning is stored
- plans are stored

Then future sessions can pick up the project.

### 5. Personal Context Repository ("Life OS")

Marc, Diego, and others described variants of this.

Pattern:

```
Personal repo
  ├── roadmap
  ├── notes
  ├── status history
  ├── templates
  ├── writing style guidance
  └── project context
```

Used as:

- personal memory
- status report generation
- project continuity
- writing assistance

This was one of the more interesting emergent practices.

### 6. Attractor/Subgraph-Oriented Design

Brian repeatedly returned to this idea.

The workflow is:

```
Useful behavior
  ↓
Extract subgraph
  ↓
Reuse subgraph
  ↓
Compose larger workflows
```

Rather than building monolithic systems.

He specifically described:

- Wiki Weaver
- Repo Weaver
- Team Pulse pieces

as collections of reusable subgraphs.

The goal is to build reusable primitives that can be recombined later.

### 7. Build for Yourself, Then Package

This was a strategic workflow discussed repeatedly.

Instead of:

```
Have idea
  ↓
Build product
```

the preferred pattern is:

```
Need something ourselves
  ↓
Build it
  ↓
Use it
  ↓
Improve it
  ↓
Package it
```

Candidate examples:

- Wiki Weaver
- Repo Weaver
- Amplifier Agent
- Amplifier Online
- PR Reviewer

The team was actively asking:

> What are we already building that could be turned into something others could use?

### 8. Samuel's Self-Improving Reviewer Workflow

Probably the most novel workflow discussed.

```
Review Loop
PR
  ↓
Review using rubric

Learning Loop
Missed bug
  ↓
Fix committed
  ↓
Analyze cause
  ↓
Propose rubric update
  ↓
Human reviews update
  ↓
Rubric improved
```

Instead of retraining a model, the system evolves the review rubric.

Several people reacted positively because it turns engineering experience into something durable.

Key philosophy:

> Every escaped defect should teach the reviewer something.

### 9. Self-Improving Processes (not just code reviewers)

The team generalized Samuel's approach beyond PR review.

The pattern becomes:

```
Work performed
  ↓
Failures occur
  ↓
Failures analyzed
  ↓
Process updated
```

Potential targets:

- prompts
- workflows
- evaluation criteria
- pipelines
- review systems

The idea is that the process itself evolves over time.

### 10. Historical Replay / Time-Travel Evaluation

Brian described replaying older states of systems.

Pattern:

```
Go back to past state
  ↓
Hide solution
  ↓
Re-run workflow
  ↓
Measure results
```

Used for:

- regression testing
- evaluating automation
- determining whether new approaches would have found the same solution

Several people seemed excited by this.

### 11. AI-First Team Workflow (Team Pulse Vision)

This was the broader Team Pulse vision.

The idea isn't "AI coding."

It's:

```
Meetings
Chats
Repos
PRs
Tasks
Goals
  ↓
Shared team memory
  ↓
AI coordination layer
  ↓
Team assistance
```

Brian repeatedly emphasized:

- team-level awareness
- team-level context
- team-level [@orchestration](project:ea68d9fd-278f-4908-a2b3-81c97de756da)

Rather than just individual copilots.

This appears to be the strategic direction behind Team Pulse.

### 12. Multi-Agent Review and Debate

Another recurring theme.

Instead of:

```
One model
  ↓
One answer
```

the workflow becomes:

```
Problem
  ↓
Multiple reviewers
  ↓
Independent critiques
  ↓
Comparison
  ↓
Human decision
```

Examples:

- Council
- Samuel's review lenses
- parallel evaluators

The team appears to have developed a strong preference for independent perspectives plus human judgment over a single monolithic agent.

### 13. Knowledge Capture and Dissemination

The later discussion added an important workflow that wasn't obvious earlier.

Several people (especially Devis, Marc, Brian) talked about the problem:

> We discover useful techniques, but they remain trapped in individual sessions.

Desired workflow:

```
Discovery
  ↓
Capture
  ↓
Summarize
  ↓
Publish
  ↓
Team learns
```

Examples discussed:

- stories
- announcements
- daily updates
- Team Pulse surfacing useful practices

A major insight was that the team now has many valuable workflows, but sharing them remains too manual.

## My synthesis

If I condense the entire meeting into a few core themes, the team has converged on four meta-workflows:

**Evaluation-driven development**

- Outcomes first
- Evaluate everything

**Persistent context**

- Workspaces
- Repositories
- Context intelligence
- Long-running sessions

**Self-improving systems**

- Reviewers improve themselves
- Processes improve themselves
- AI workflows improve themselves

**Packaging proven practices**

- Solve real problems
- Use internally
- Extract reusable patterns
- Share them with others

Shared by [@Brian](person:6f790c53-9404-4b7e-86de-4498a071899d):

- I want to reset expectations clearly and directly.
- Each of you is on this team because I’ve been given an objective and there’s more work than I can personally execute. You were brought here to deliver specific outcomes that I delegate.
- Your value here is directly tied to how well you take work off my plate and deliver exactly what’s assigned—cleanly, predictably, and with good judgment about scope.
- This is not a side-quest role. Doing good work that isn’t what I asked for still creates cost if it pulls focus from what I need delivered. Expanding asks, redefining the problem, or building adjacent systems without alignment works against the goal.
- If an execution-focused role like this feels constraining, that’s okay—but it means this may not be the right seat right now, and we should talk about a better fit elsewhere.
- Autonomy here is earned. It comes from consistent delivery, staying on target, communicating clearly, and producing steady results with low overhead. When that happens, the outcome is exactly what many of you want—and what I want: more ownership, more trust, and more room to run.
- Going forward, especially as we come back in January, the expectation is simple: snap to delivering what I distribute. If that’s not happening, we address it quickly. If it continues, we make a role or team change.
- This isn’t about control. It’s about leverage. When execution is tight, everyone wins.
- Note from [@Sam](person:d52e9454-21e6-44ed-bae7-66d750ccb17b): Not only are they to be doing the work you ask, they had better be doing it the RIGHT way, or at least trying. No more going off into the weeds doing code reviews or whatever (this is about up-leveling our engagement with our AI tools, leveraging/offloading more, getting away directing at the code level, etc.).

His followup:

- Sam and I were debugging where the friction is coming in from.
- I'm disrespected. I want to be a partner and I'm a resource.
- "specific outcomes" -- right. There's no specificity in most things here.

My reflection:

- The friction is Brian's brain. It's expensive.

"I’ve been given an objective" -- is this a general statement that you are in general given objectives by Sam... or is this a specific objective you can state?

- Kevin: Go find ways to use models and approaches to achieve more.
- Brian: Pull in context from Medium. Build up more valuable context over time (synthesis).
- Sam: Do that but build up more meta-cognitive ([@amplifier](project:d5f8fb75-ba6d-4a26-9795-0b42c1a139fb)). We believe that meta-cognitive recipes are the way to capture the how and why of what we are thinking and to be able to leverage them and hand them off to others. 
- Brian: Amplifier Claude showed that context can be saved in directories and it is helpful. We are making primitives that allow the LLMs to set up capture our meta-cognitive instructions. How do we leverage everyone elses things (plugins, bundles, etc.) (amplifier-core).

My thought: I've been helping with this objective all along but not been listened to or given enough credit. Brian doesn't listen to my ideas.

Now he's describing how he set up his terminal over a few days to be more productive. It sounds exactly like what I was doing with [@Lakehouse](project:79287625-ebda-433d-af86-cab2dd5b8277). His problem with Lakehouse is that it comes across as a side-quest that wasn't authorized. I view it though, essentially, just like his thing... small investments over time to make me more productive.

Things that make me more productive with Lakehouse:

- A daemon let's me add background processes easily. Scheduled background prompts make automation simple and powerful.
- Projects make context management simpler. I can edit context (AGENTS.md) easily in the interface.
- The interface lets me modify profiles and configuration for them easily. In combination with modules in a registry (instead of being spread out throughout the internet), this makes experimentation with different profile configurations (mount plans) fast.
- Behaviors and context is composable. This makes tool and context experimentation faster for me. Context, in particular, being composable really helps me develop context improvements when needed.
- Built-in trace and log tools make it easy to see what is going on.
- Easy to track sessions and fast to re-enter (better than amplifier -c)
- All profiles being precompiled makes debugging with breakpoints easy to understand.
- Generated mount plans are cached so I can both see what is happening and can move them to the cli or other scripts easily.
- I can switch profiles mid-session (and soon behaviors). This will allow me experiment inside a single session.
- All state is in files, again, making it easy to see what's going on and to migrate it when things change... I don't lose work.
- In general, building this really helped me understand what is in the cli vs core and how exactly the core works.

body:
### Things I enjoy working with

- Engineering

  - Analyzing and making shit.

- Information Design

  - Capturing the essence of systems with information modeling.

- Macho

  - Some connection with cool, attractive, exciting/dangerous that
    is powerfully admirable, interesting and attractive.

- Culture-Moda Influence

  - Finger on the pulse. People turn their heads and watch...
    learning something about themselves and the world. They are
    drawn, attracted to to the new thing and feel compelled to get
    involved, to interact with it personally themselves.

- Money/Resources

  - Streamlined resource delivery.

- The Human Condition

  - The real working of the human animal (evolutionary psychology),
    the embracing of the full human (Jungian psychology),
    de-mythologizing and embracing our place in the universe
    (environmental), understanding violence.

### On Personal Style

[I can dress the way I want to be, right now.\
\
What is the correct word for this:\
Unconventional but not careless. Charming but not feminine.
Hint-of-danger, virile charm. Fun loving but not silly. More put
together than uncouth... able to move in cultural circles. Yet without
emasculation. Intelligent. Subversive.\
\
Rakish is too "debonair". Raffish is to "devil-may-care", too
"rogue".]

### On Being Open

Any choice of profession I make will inevitably cut me off from part of
my desire. Only running a company purely devoted to realizing my
individual vision would prevent this. My vision would have to be
singular, precise, piercing. The other option would be to cut to the
chase. The whole point of chasing this type of "becoming what I truly
am" desire chasing is to find my "place" in the world where I will be
esteemed for precisely what my strengths are and where that esteem will
give me what I want in life (opportunity, wealth, excitement). Instead
of "building" my way there, perhaps I can "be" my way there. Open
myself in such a way as I am not defined by what I have built, but
instead am defined by what I relationally am... by my humanity...
being open to the type of people I enjoy... creative, realist,
exciting, sexy people.

One thing is for sure... no matter which profession I choose... this
is only the "building" work. There remains a more significant matter
of "being"... developing the way I dress, relate, think, emote...
the type of person I want to be.

My utopian relationship philosophy allows for me to be friends with her

If someone else is meeting my needs, either add that to the relationship

title: Why stay despite misalignment
body:
[@Jen](person:79ed28f0-e91e-42aa-99a2-3d50bbaab49c) has wanted "attunement" for 22+ years. I have tried to give it to
her for 20+ years.

My experience is keep trying and failing, so we have no relationship.

Her experience is we have a relationship, but an unsatisfying one. If I
get better at attuneness, she would be happy.

She says attunement is why all my relationships at work are bad.

How can I be so productive yet so unattuned?

Perhaps it is selfish of me to stay. Know my strengths and weaknesses.

It is a value question, what would mean to be successful at [@Ximor](organization:a5026bba-8ce8-4576-aa3a-14db0cad7ca3)? I
suppose by developing a model in extensive coordination with everyone
(crack that nut!), by listening more... bring order... help organize
some design problems... in short, by applying all my strengths to help
build a strong company.

But what about my objectives, my true life? Does it make sense for me to
align myself to Ximor so much? Only if I believe in the mission, and the
virtue of those whom I work with. Or perhaps if I love them enough.

What are Jen and I's mission? Kids' parenting. Do I respect her virtue?

Courage Yes Love? Yes

Wisdom No

Discipline No

Justice Questionable

Love? A bit

So why do I stay?

Our home brings joy to my life.

When she is around, I am delighted, safe, content.

I don't want to harm my children, especially on the edge of such an
important transition.

"When I let go of what I am, I become what I might be" -- [@Lao Tzu](person:c1d660e4-1cf7-46a5-ab50-35287392f984)

title: Hustle vs stability
body:
TTM: This may be the key to my lack of success. Slow and steady progress
is not a thing for me. Fits and starts and massive outlays of energy and
no rest and task to task and next big thing. I manage the things I need
to, but don't manage the things I should. No savings. No investments.
No improvement plans. I don't feel like I deserve the good things... a
nice place; financial security; a job I love; relationships that
reward. Instead, I believe what I have is where to set my bar: 60K
debt; little savings; an ok house; an ok wife; ok kids; ok job.

The idea of a store; being a merchant appeals for the detail-focused
nature of it. I fantasize about counting all the pennies; arranging the
shelves just so. The idea of putting in the work and having the payoff
is so appealing. Maybe I'm just tired of hustling. Or getting too old.
I don't want a [@Jordan](person:3ae7ef1e-26b3-4645-9593-24777f162348) or a [@Gena](person:42f31ff5-95b8-4092-b73d-8a0cdffeb49d) or a [@JB](person:7265dc0f-70c7-4138-8611-bd8a317e201e) or a [@Chris](person:ed49ba8d-3965-4b80-b588-f79b4edfed65) or a [@Scott](person:da8e50a4-4fcc-4495-a099-b17732da06e1) to tell
me what to do... to have me bust my balls for an immediate
compensation... but no long-term stability.

If I'd save I'd get the long-term stability. If I balanced my life
better, I'd not get so tired of hustling. I'd have time for the other
things I care about.

Or I can be my own boss again. I loved that; I really did. I need learn
how to bring others in; to be ok making the huge bucks. Hiring.
Managing. Thank you [@Atlas](organization:d8101bf2-9e7b-409d-b820-3e2aefd3689b) for that experience.

Major stressors: keeping Atlas platform running; taking Atlas platform
into next gen; Jordan; managing team; home happiness; long-term
financial well-being; children being successful.

This I need to solve: thoughts building on one another rather than
herky-jerky. I need a place for journaling; a place for plans. Planning
needs to have high-level goals and metrics. I tried this on paper
before... but that is shit. The one-pager didn't work either.

title: (Wed) Third breakup: The text. Jen wants to try again
body:
Has a conversation with [@Mav](person:11bd1888-7d7a-4e9a-885e-5b520d6e707a) about this Sat morn... the crux was I want
to keep dating but am more autonomous that she seems to want, I want to
spend more time on my legacy... her reaction was ish "You want the good
without the bad" and she basically kicked me out of her place. She then
said she wanted time to think, attended a b-day party for [@Trey](person:c0e0e416-395a-4b3f-ae3b-e08370770af9) w/ [@Phil](person:520138a2-a693-433f-ab2d-0fbe191ece6a).
On Tue morn she finally got back to me via a Telegram message: _"Hey,
thanks for giving me space and time to reflect. I have much more clarity
now. I would like to break up and take some substantial time apart to
move on and heal. I'm grateful for the many fun times we've shared, and
I can only imagine the incredible things you'll achieve in your career
and for your legacy!"_ No word since.

I've been mostly relieved. But sad. Angry now writing this that she
wouldn't/couldn't say this to me face to face. That's the main reason I
feel relieved, though, she had limited relational capability and
self-understanding. I can't expect much more from her than what she is
giving.

Met w/ [@Jen](person:79ed28f0-e91e-42aa-99a2-3d50bbaab49c) last night. She wants to "give it another try". Part of me
wants to, too, but I'm tired of people not loving me well (both of them,
ha!). I should probably just stay alone unless I ever find someone who
gets me, is healthy, I am attractive to, and adds to my life. I feel
lonely already... but am interested to see how it develops... will I
invest more in my network and aspirations? So far I seem to be...
cleaned, cleared out my email, set up a date w/ [@Chapman](person:1485a6fd-2b75-4d41-b8aa-6f5970cdd3a8), architecting,
relaxing... and eating too much and smoking and staying up too late...
but I already am driven to improve them. With no one else's image of me,
and no one else to keep satisfied, I find I am kind and motivating to
myself.

Jen's offer isn't timeless, though. She offers sex, non-monogamy,
limited expectations, leaning into showing me love, in exchange for me
being her primary partner (jealousy about being cut out, but not jealous
about sharing).

Had a conversation with Voltaire and Socrates yesterday on romantic
love.

Later...

She wrote "I'm grateful for the many fun times we've shared", but I'm
grateful for more.

title: MADE: Exploration — Strategy (the what)
body:
Understood—I’ll merge the **recent guidance from [@Brian](person:6f790c53-9404-4b7e-86de-4498a071899d)** with the **previous strategic framing**, keeping older content only if it’s still relevant and not superseded. Here’s a consolidated, up-to-date view:

***

## **[@MADE: Exploration](area:57e87863-7ee7-410d-b25d-096c29474fbd) Objectives — Combined Strategic Lens**

### **1. Anchor on Outcome-Driven Workflows and Context Management (Recent Priority)**

*   Shift from feature sprawl to **workflows that deliver clear outcomes**.
*   Build **context-aware systems** to simplify collaboration and reduce cognitive load.
*   Standardize templates and philosophy docs for consistency.  
    *(Recent syncs and Brian’s feedback)*

***

### **2. Recipes as the Backbone for Reliability and Extensibility**

*   Recipes remain central: **structured, reusable workflows** for automation and [@orchestration](project:ea68d9fd-278f-4908-a2b3-81c97de756da).
*   Enable customization and extension of reference implementations.
*   Support metacognition and automated documentation regeneration.  
    *(Recent guidance + earlier roadmap continuity)*

***

### **3. [@Amplifier](project:d5f8fb75-ba6d-4a26-9795-0b42c1a139fb) and Orchestration Experiments**

*   Evolve **Amplifier** into a modular orchestration layer.
*   Experiment with orchestrator patterns (foreman-worker, observer) to coordinate multi-agent setups.
*   Validate reliability through **tests and conformance suites** before scaling.  
    *(Recent standups + Brian’s emphasis on controlled change)*

***

### **4. High-Impact Assistant Concepts (Still Core)**

*   **Synthesis Assistant**: Automate summarization and synthesis across docs and conversations.
*   **Semantic Workbench**: Enhance productivity through AI-powered workflow augmentation.
*   These remain strategic pillars for exploration, even as orchestration gains focus.  
    *(Earlier roadmap + still active demos)*

***

### **5. Collaboration After Individual Utility**

*   Delay advanced collaboration features until single-user workflows prove value.
*   Keep everything in a **shared repo** for unified vision and onboarding ease.  
    *(Recent sync notes)*

***

### **6. [@Knowledge Transfer](project:a384618f-96c6-4ad0-ae79-6f43ec54f2b5) and Lightweight Capture**

*   Invest in **Knowledge Transfer Assistants** and synthesis tools.
*   Capture learnings in a lightweight, reusable way to avoid rediscovery.  
    *(Recent demos + older meta-objective still relevant)*

***

### **7. Influence Through Demos and Vision**

*   Continue producing **short, impactful demos** and vision docs for leadership and partner teams.
*   Use storytelling and phased recommendations to shape strategy.  
    *(Older roadmap guidance still valid for external impact)*

***

## **In Short**

Brian’s current framing builds on earlier objectives but sharpens focus on:

*   **Outcome-driven workflows**
*   **Recipes as a foundation**
*   **Amplifier orchestration and reliability**
*   **Knowledge transfer and controlled evolution**
    while keeping **assistant prototypes and strategic influence** in play.

title: A Reddit post on our RA journey
body:
Posted this on /r/relationship_anarchy and felt silly so edited it down.
This is the long version:

Hmm, I've been thinking about this for a few days now. I just don't
think there's any way to faithfully sum up and our story is so unique
(I think?) that I'm not sure how much it would translate to anyone
else's situation. I'll just throw out some thoughts to try to give
some sort of an answer.

We married young and were each others first significant relationship.
We've always struggled with our relationship not meeting all our needs
and not living up to the "ideal". We have chronic complaints with one
another, almost entirely due to our attachment styles... she leaning
anxious, me leaning avoidant. But we both have been, for the most part,
fully invested. We had a horrible time in year 3. Then in year 7. Year
10 was so traumatizing that I think we both have been unwilling to be
that "dramatic" since then. We work hard on ourselves as individuals
and together. We deeply love and respect each other at the core... but
it's never been enough for either of us to feel wholly satisfied.

About a year ago I really started sitting with the idea that, after 24
years, I need to be honest that it just wasn't likely anymore that I
was going to be able to change in a meaningful way to somehow become
what she really wants. So, I wasn't going to get what I wanted either,
then. I started planning for divorce.

Then, about 9 months ago, I ate mushrooms for the first time. It was a
life-changing experience on many fronts, but in relation to this topic,
I was just filled with so much love and compassion for her, and for us.
I remember really feeling how tragic our story would be if it were only
that we tried for 25 years then failed... that it was all a monumental
waste of life. And, anyway, I just really love her... I remembered how
I loved her 25 years ago, and it hadn't changed... a strong admiration
and wonder-filled kind of love. Also, I got in touch with just how
strange it was to "own" someone through a marriage contract. I
realized (deeply) I did not want to own her, I've never wanted to own
her, I just wanted to be with her. This really cemented the idea for me
that I wanted to both love her and let the expectations and demands of
our marriage contract go.

I shared this experience with her, so I guess you can say the idea has
been in the air since then. The idea that we can love one another and
not love the idea of marriage, and that we might not actually be able to
meet each other's needs in every way.

We gave marriage counseling another go, really focused on [@Tatkin](person:3ab92b91-66ac-4831-9cad-8f35956fe14f) and
[@Gottman](person:a264af57-31c2-47d8-abb3-5e9a4068cda8). We got much better at listening to each other and coregulating
when either of us were triggered. Throughout these past months, she's
been in the position of wanting keep things together while I've
remained in the position of being willing to let things end if we can't
muster the change both of us want.

After the holidays she was the one to bring up this latest conversation.
We had both been reading and discussing patriarchy's effect on society
and marriage. She had also read Polysecure. Some combination of my trip,
honest discussion and listening in therapy, feminist theory, and now,
connections between relational style and new forms of intimate
relationships brought her to suggesting she was ready to throw the
expectations out and create a new agreement with each other from a place
that feels most true to each of us individually. She said she expects to
always want to be in relationship with me but wants us to feel more free
to create something new.

I totally agreed and speed-read Polysecure, which I think introduced me
to RA. It was so enlivening to find in RA a way of relating that made
sense to me, almost like I've come home. In retrospect, it seems like
we've both been trying to find our way here for a very, very long time.

The only advice I would maybe pass your way would be consider not
talking about RA directly right out of the gate, but to bring up the
aspects of it you are drawn to and would like to see in your
relationship. E.g. love is abundant... how narrowly we define love when
it has so many aspects... there are so many types of intimacy and how
rare it is to find someone to be everything. Or perhaps, how important
it is in relationships to maintain a sense of independence to truly
love... that love must be freely offered, not contractually obligated,
to be true. From a different perspective, contemplating the entitlement
that poisons relationships. One more thing... I avoided sharing some of
my transparent thoughts and doubts for so many years because I thought
they would be hurtful. I was right. But, at least its a respectful,
honest hurt vs the hidden, resentful, gaslighting, poisonous kind of
hurt. As I learn to be transparent with my potentially hurtful thoughts
and feelings, I think I'm also learning to be more gracious,
optimistic, and loving. Instead of focusing my unspoken anger and
disappointment, I find myself focusing on how to comfort while taking
more responsibility in generating positive forward movement. Kind and
tender to both her and myself, while not backing away from integrity. I
think it's helpful to remember the kind of person we want to be when
entering into these discussions.

title: Academy initiation
body:
- a story:

- opens in a highly-competive academy. 100 students in advanced, state
  of the art coursework from emotional, to leadership, to science,
  engineering, technical, ethical. This academy, you understand,
  produces the leaders of tommorrow. some portion of the cohort are
  entirely outclassed and know it. a smaller group of 18 or so are
  identified as the best of the best and competition is fierce to
  become the valedictorians.

- to much buzz, "the dedicates" and "the elect" arrive. they
  dedicates were the previous years valedictorians, whom no one has
  seen since graduation, while the elect were the years previous
  still. they are all celebrities, almost revered, universally
  esteemed. their arrival is a celebration of news from the colonies,
  refreshed supplies, and the safe return of the dedicates whom will
  be staying for only a week before setting off again. the elects, in
  a solemn, and extravagant ceremony are made citizens, to much joy
  and tears.

- graduation, the six valedictorians are announced. They are given a
  new name, "the initiates". The cohort enter their fleet, 12 to a
  shuttle, the initiates with the dedicates. With tears and
  celebration, the fleet launches into the wild towards their assigned
  colonies, their years of incubation at an end.

- the intiates are left for a time to their wild anticipation as the
  dedicates excuse themselves. when they return, the initiates are
  informed, in an exhaustive exposition, that there are no other
  colonies and the rest of their class has been euthanized, now known
  collectively as "the returned".

- they arrive at a processing outpost where, for the next year, the
  initiates are taught the ethics of the system while processing the
  bodies of the returned into new supplies. skin turned to leather,
  meat reduced to amino acids then protein food, medicines extracted
  from glands, scientific data collected for health research, bones
  used as chiton. there are none of these natural resources on the
  planet on which they have been stranded for 14 generations. this,
  indeed, is the only way to survive and the only hope for making the
  breakthroughs required to escape the moon, return to their habitable
  neighbor, and continue civilization. there are sizeable elements for
  fuel and repairs, but they have not yet unlocked the method to
  convert them.

- a year later, they return, are celebrated, celebate the dedicates
  becoming citizens, and board their shuttle for their last real rite
  of entry.

- they retire to the room where they each, simultaneously press the
  buttons to euthanize the new class.

- this book speaks to the ethics of "ethical" systems of control,
  the struggle of colluding with them, the sense of futility in trying
  to escape them, the ache to maintain purity, and the final numbing
  of surrender to it. ultimately, we are constrained by our
  environment, and our only response is to advance, push through, as
  quickly as possible... a statement against trancendentalist
  fantasy, or ethical ludditry.

title: RA? Split finances first.
body:
Split financial accounts. Why?

- To address my resentment at having to spend my life on things I
  don't want.

- To provide a sense of autonomy for me to change my future.

- She doesn't save. I have been disadvantaged in access to our joint
  accounts. [@Jen](person:79ed28f0-e91e-42aa-99a2-3d50bbaab49c) spends more money than I do while I carry pressure to
  ensure the family has enough income. Jen has never concerned herself
  with retirement savings or long-term financial planning.

- She spends. Jen spends our money with relatively (to me) less
  consideration of cost. As she has not been personally sacrificing to
  produce income, she has become insensitive to the value of money.
  This builds resentment in that I am sacrificing my life for shit I
  don't want (supplements, treatments, organics, beauty products) ...
  to the tune of 14K per month (5-10k/month beyond what we should be
  spending).

- She won't work. Jen, since marriage, has never had a full-time job
  (except [@Crusade](organization:c1f0f2bd-fc1e-4a83-9ebd-e85c88e0d72f)). Even when I paid for two degrees, childcare, and
  was responsible for half of the chores she always worked part-time
  as a therapist and has worked minimally over the past two years
  while she has been engaging on spiritual and intellectual pursuits.

- Our desire for the future at odds. She speaks of "us" buying a
  second house in [@Joshua Tree](location:817b7b25-c6eb-40e3-82d7-1f1a8ec954df) and working throughout retirement. I
  want to be a minimalist and travel and retire early. She assumes
  we'll keep paying for [@Sinead](person:72a05873-c2c7-4de6-b5e2-ae6c2abcf2d3) and [@Fiona](person:40f1bbfa-f375-4a65-84d9-1290fd02a3c7), assumes we will provide what
  she felt entitled to from her parents: mortgage down payments and
  inheritances.

- She is ungrateful. She gets angry when I suggest she and the kids
  should wash the dishes. She says she is tired of cooking even though
  she works two to three days a week. She complains that I am too
  concerned with money... that I don't have enough balance. She
  expects to be an independent feminist while refusing to take
  responsibility of her own livelihood. She bashes science daily even
  though it feeds her. She bashes finance as boring even though I've
  doubled her retirement account in a year. She bashes capitalism and
  ownership while living in a million-dollar house eating organic food
  shipped with [@Amazon](organization:1a057d38-38a4-4f7b-9747-10d8496f2e4b) Prime. She gives our money away to her causes
  without telling me so I can share in the good feels. She complains
  about me not loving her enough, discounting entirely how I express
  my love through providing.

- She has unfair expectations of me: that I will work indefinitely to
  pay for everything while she does what she wants.

So, now that she feels the real pressure of making money, I expect she
will:

- Have more respect for the challenge of balancing need with desire
  (why I think about money all the time).
- Will start to make money.
- Will stop spending so much money on food.
- Will stop spending so much money on healthcare (will find magically
  that she doesn't need as many supplements as she used to).
- Will value the things she has more.
- _Will resent me for making so much more money than her and not
  giving it to her. The discussion of why men owe women will now never
  cease. The story of her being a household martyr will take on new
  life... even though I was the one sacrificing._

title: Deciding whether to split
body:
She wants split. I'm trying to decide by tonight.

At the bar last night I felt so dreadful about the idea of trying to
find love.

_That's not where love is found. That's where you play_. _Love is
found in pieces, cast across the earth and carried in. You have been
without the love you need for a long time. The thought of losing what
you do have is terrifying. So, open your heart to love, dearest [@Paul](person:0b085c55-5431-4cd4-89d1-af1bf1b5e817).
Take in the sun's fiery kiss, the trees' eternal the sea's endless
parade. Take in the soil that supports you, the water that restores you,
the air that penetrates you like a lover. And take in the sparkling eyes
of someone who trusts you and calls you friend. Take in the admiration
of your colleagues. And, most of all, take in your self. You are so
very, very, loved. I know your every step, every heartache, every
victory. I've wept, and cheered, and have been so proud, with you, for
you, of you. Be loved, dearest Paul. Be loved. May your heart be full
and remember while breathing you are never alone._

Stories of alimony bondage fight with the safety of keeping things open.
Sign an agreement now, but why keep things open?

- For me to fuck around and see if I want [@Jen](person:79ed28f0-e91e-42aa-99a2-3d50bbaab49c) again?

- To see if we can imagine a new way of relating that fulfills us
  both---she likes space.

What about this:

- Companionship

  - The friends we were

    - Hang out. Support. Laugh. Dream.

  - Visit from the faun when you need him.

  - Support.

- Autonomy, so I can have my other needs met, and we cherish what we
  have.

  - ENM/RA

  - Divorce

  - Move out

If that's the picture, why not do it now? Then, as friends, if we ever
decide to become exclusive or live with each other again, we can.

[@Jen](person:79ed28f0-e91e-42aa-99a2-3d50bbaab49c) didn't want this in the past because she valued certainty more than
companionship from me.

---

I want to be family. I want to still have holidays. Birthdays.
Celebrations. I want to be a part of [@Sean](person:4d2f1f09-7526-42e6-95b5-203576234e18), Miss, and the boys lives. I
want to help with the house. I want to go on trips. I want to consider
having a place in [@Joshua Tree](location:817b7b25-c6eb-40e3-82d7-1f1a8ec954df). I want to catch up. Have coffee dates.
Know what's going in in your life.

I want to have autonomy. To follow my own paths spiritually,
philosophically, relationally. Currently, essential parts of my life are
locked up in marriage. I can't pursue them without creating more
conflict, more distance in our intimacy, more loneliness.

You have expressed for a long time now that you want space, a removal of
expectations, that you want to be valued for what you bring rather than
feeling disappointment for what I'm missing. I think we both want
autonomy. Neither of us wants to lose the stability we've worked so
hard to create.

It's deep intimacy we never realized and I don't think it's primarily
either of ours fault. I think we just can't complete each other here
fully, we are wired differently.

Let's have autonomy. Let's let the demands and expectation of intimacy
go. Let's keep our family. Let's keep our friendship.

You've said I'm not the kind of friend you would choose and without
intimacy, you wouldn't want to be my friend. But I do want to be your
friend, so I'm asking, can that be enough for you?

I don't believe a separation would change what I want around intimacy,
and it wouldn't answer whether we can be intimate while living
together. So, I think we need to proceed with divorce and moving out and
focus on being family. If, with distance, and with friendship we find a
new kind of intimacy developing, we can choose to lean in again, be
lovers again, but on our own terms, and without the patriarchy telling
us what we should be doing.

---

philosophically, relationally. Currently, significant parts of my life
are locked up in marriage, I can't pursue them without creating more
conflict or more distance in our intimacy

- I want to live minimally

- I want my relationships with others to be embodied, physical,
  sexual, without censor

- I want to maintain momentum on my own spiritual paths without having
  them undermined as compromised by patriarchy or consumed by your
  paths of misogyny and patriarchy

- I want my life to be out of the house, in the night, off the
  screens, interacting with society

- In my space, I want to be surrounded by full expressions of my self
  (music, art, furnishings, atmosphere) masculinity, sensuality,
  exploration, fun

- I want to be naked, an embodied sanctuary and canvas

She despairs when a relationship isn't giving her what she needs. She
feels like she is trying so hard. But in reality, she's not asking for
what she needs (e.g. don't leave me at a bar, fuck me, etc.). On
Valentine's day I told her I didn't want to keep talking about work,
that it seemed like she was avoiding being connected to me, she shame
spiraled, saying "I always mess it all up!". She was unable to hear my
need (wanting to connect). She was unable to voice her need (wanting to
feel treasured?). It resulted in her saying "I want to just go to
sleep".

So this is the type of shit, not being able to connect for some time,
that makes her think "Phil might be a better option for me"?

I have to unpack this in depth with her. I need to know:

**?** Why couldn't we connect (it wasn't just all me). I wanted to have
sex but she, busy with work, kept removing herself from my apt, even
when I had obviously put effort into making it beautiful, and we had
talked earlier in the day about wanting each other. Very fucking
confusing.

**?** Why did she shut down on Valentines day when I told her I was
hoping to connect more (it wasn't just all me)

**?** Why didn't she break up with me before scoping out Phil? Will she
be ok with me scoping out other women if I am dissatisfied with her? And
if the women really like me and hide their interactions from me from
her, and I tell her that I was actually interested in them, would she
still be friends with them?

Let's play this forward and imagine that we all were continuously
hedging our bets in relationships. Always checking out potential
partners (she did this with Mike, remember) when she is unable to get
what she wants in relationship (from me, monogamy, from Mike, an end to
secrets). We just keep hanging out in a fucked relationship because (a)
it might change, and (b) it might be the best you can do. But then you
start to give up on A and you want to see what else is out there. One
route is to make this optimal... always be interacting with new people
and sizing them up. Change quickly... you'll over time be with the best
person. The other route, which I am arguing for is: try to work with
your partner to meet your needs, decide if the dissatisfaction reaches a
certain threshold, and if it does, break up with them. I believe Mav
doesn't like this option because she would rather have a fucked up
relationship than no relationship. That's why she would totally take a
loser like Phil, or [@Dan](person:26343b14-5fbc-46dd-8268-d638cc5ef953), or [@Nick](person:652940bb-c99a-4ba9-a09a-eeb728c03372), or Mike... or, apparently, me.

**?** Why does Mav stay with losers?

**?** Why is she ok with losers? Low self-esteem, sure, but why that
kind of esteem... ah... because she has the sunday scaries, is
petrified at not measuring up everywhere, has an abusive father, a rib
sticking out, and is almost disabled with her back.

**\>** I need her to take point on building her own esteem, and
resolving these issues she believes make her unworthy to have a good
lover.

**\>** So if she does want to be with me, if our relationship isn't
working for her, I need her to engage with _me_ and not just scope
someone else out. I understand how this was actually a decent tactic for
someone like me who wants to have open relationships, although even in
that scenario, ENM would require much more transparent communication, to
the point of "you make me sad and I don't think you want me, so I'm
going to go hang out with Phil and see if I like him better"\--at least
that would give me an chance to defend myself. But in the case of
dating, that's just breaking a commitment with a partner. That should
only happen if the partner says "I will not, or cannot meet your need
here" after you have made it crystal clear how important of a need it
is.

So, if we start dating, I will need to ask her "Do you want to be
friends with someone who was not a good friend to me? Do you want to go
to Portland with them?"

Here's another thing that bothers me... she talks about guys chasing
her all the fucking time, but the one time I tell her a girl was into
me, she is hurt?? Fuck that.

Also, who was it that she wanted to keep up with her Instagram account?
Gotta be Phil or she would have told me, right?

body:

  dating. Ambivalent about all of them including jeanie.

  [@San Diego](location:5e412cfd-6b01-4367-85fd-9082dd93345b) with [@Stan](person:8fb00d67-0ddc-43d2-8228-1c6527fff3b0).

- Spending time listening to my heart... what do you want... what do
  you like... what do you want to be?

- Read "When Nietzsche Wept" with thoughts, "What is the meaning of
  this obsession?", "Become who you are", "Amor fati (thus I willed
  it)", and eternal recurrence... a particularly powerful exhortation
  to live each moment as though you will have to relive it eternally.

The most beautiful and most terrifying moments spent alone in this loft
overlooking [@the Sound](location:d86d6c95-147a-4a3e-b492-924256745cd0).

The beautiful moments of sublime peace and reflection. Easily allowing
the flow of time, feeling its lazy movement like floating down a calm
river through a world lush with life. Feeling the gratitude of safety,
no threats, no fear of the future, knowing there is time, time, time,
and it will be filled with as many moments like these as I allow. I am
in touch, now, with life, the unchanging vibration of living, which has
animated every joyful moment across my years, uniting this room with my
childhood bedroom. The same air wafting through the windows, the same
sunlight illuminating the floorboards, then scuffed, crayon and
foot-polished oak, now modern urban loft textile.

The sun shifts behind a cloud, and my heart skips. The panic prods. I am
alone and have made a mess of everything. Spent 30 years chasing a
technical dream of meaning, abandoned my wife, fumbled a lover. This,
the first (covid-enforced) week of solitude in... 29 years (!!). I am
alone, and I have not found the meaning I've searched for, the
relationships I've longed for, the impact I've desired, the joy that
would make any of this worthwhile. I failed to develop the courage to
speak clearly and truly to the world. I have no self.

I bob between these extremes, of myself then cowering, from one moment
to the next, like some tragic waltz... up to the mountain, down to the
valley, up to power, down to powerlessness, up to love, down to pity, up
to vision, down to obsession, up to self-love, down to self-loathing. I
am so grateful for this dance, at this moment. Before this week of
solitude, it was a dirge... a decrepit march through a cold, wet
wasteland.

A core forms in my solitude. I remember what it is to be me, not what
the world, others, my fears would have me be. So, what am I that brings
such joy, and needs to be spoken?

I am a unique expression of the universe never to be repeated, the stars
dance to see me live full.

I am an eruption of organic matter playing out its encoding to stake its
place in the ecosystem and thrive long enough to inject its experiment
into the next round.

I am a thought in another's head, a feeling in their body, a part of
concentric circles of butterfly-effect influence.

I am an infant, a child, an adolescent, a man, a crone, a corpse,
energy.

I am a creator. An innovator.

I am a friend, a lover, a threat, a demon.

There is no I.

[@Paul](person:0b085c55-5431-4cd4-89d1-af1bf1b5e817)... just be... just be... just be...

Standard Azure docs are written for the world outside the Microsoft corporate tenant. Inside it, they don't just fall short — they mislead: they tell you to create a client secret you're not allowed to have, and they never warn you about the failures that show a ✓ in the portal but a ✗ in the token. What it is:
A platform-agnostic expert for building on Azure inside the hardened Microsoft Entra corporate tenant — identity, authentication, and deployment. Activate the /ms-corp-azure-expert mode and you unlock the azure-tenant-expert agent, a context sink carrying the full knowledge base so it never crowds your root session.

- The zero-secrets thesis — why client secrets are unavailable, and how EasyAuth + MSAL.js work without them
- The -api / -client two-registration app model
- Roles vs. groups authorization, and why group claims silently vanish
- Managed identity and service-to-service auth with no secret
- Microsoft Graph / SharePoint (M365) integration from a browser SPA
- Silent-failure debugging — trust the token, not the portal

# [NEW] Amplifier Online — ship your project to Azure from your repo, and an AI bundle that drives it for you

Getting an app running on Azure inside the corp tenant is a slog of app registrations, image registries, EasyAuth, and CI wiring. Amplifier Online turns it into a handful of commands: a CLI + provisioner service that owns the hard Azure parts, plus an Amplifier bundle that lets your assistant run the whole thing conversationally. Here's how to get set up and ship your first project.

## Part 1 — Set up (once)

1. **Install the CLI** (needs `uv`):

   ```bash
   uv tool install git+https://github.com/microsoft/amplifier-online#subdirectory=cli
   ```

2. **Point it at our provisioner:**

   ```bash
   amplifier-online config
   ```
   When prompted for `service_url`, enter our internal provisioner:
   `https://amplifier-online-apim.azure-api.net`

   Config is saved to `~/.amplifier-online/config.yaml`

3. **Install the Amplifier bundle** so your assistant can drive deploys:

   ```bash
   amplifier bundle add "git+https://github.com/microsoft/amplifier-bundle-amplifier-online@main#subdirectory=behaviors/amplifier-online.yaml" --app
   ```

That's it. In any Amplifier session, run `/amplifier-online` and just describe what you want to deploy — the bundle routes the work to the `deployment-guide` agent and runs the CLI for you.

## Pick a stack

A "stack" is the deployment blueprint for your project — it decides what Azure resources get provisioned. Amplifier Online
ships several, so it's not just for one kind of app:

| Stack | What it deploys |
|-------|-----------------|
| `web-app-aca` | Container app (public web app + optional Postgres/Cosmos/Redis/Storage) |
| `web-app-awa` | Azure Web App backend + Static Web App frontend |
| `internal-service-aca` | Internal-only container app, no public ingress |
| `static-web-app` | Pure static site, no backend |
| `vm` | Private Linux VM (cloud-init, no container image) |

See the live list any time with `amplifier-online stack list`. Full per-stack details:
[docs/stacks](https://github.com/microsoft/amplifier-online/tree/main/docs/stacks)

## Part 2 — Deploy a new project

From your project repo:

```bash
amplifier-online init            # Scaffold amplifier-online.yaml from your chosen stack
                                 # (pick a stack; it fills in the image URIs for you)
# Edit amplifier-online.yaml     # Set ports / resources
amplifier-online up --dry-run    # Preview what gets provisioned
amplifier-online up              # Provision the Azure resources
amplifier-online cicd create     # Generate the GitHub deploy workflows (container stacks)
git add .github/workflows/ && git commit -m "add deploy workflows" && git push
                                 # CI builds the image → provisioner deploys it
amplifier-online status          # Check it
```

Two things worth knowing:

- **Don't hand-write `amplifier-online.yaml`** — always generate it with `amplifier-online init`. It produces a stack-correct
manifest; edit it from there.
- **For container stacks you never push to the shared registry yourself.** `git push` triggers CI, which builds and delivers
the image; the provisioner imports it and deploys. (The `vm` stack skips images entirely — you supply a `cloud-init.yaml`
instead.)

Or skip the commands entirely: in an Amplifier session with the bundle installed, run `/amplifier-online` and say "deploy this
project" — it walks the same flow with approval gates.

## Prerequisites

- `uv` (to install the CLI), Azure CLI (`az`), GitHub CLI (`gh`, for `cicd create`), Docker (local image builds)
- **No need to log in first:** the CLI uses your existing `az login` session if you have one; if not, it runs `az login` for
you, and only falls back to a browser sign-in if the Azure CLI isn't available. Note: device-code login is blocked in the corp
tenant — the normal browser flow is used.

title: Actually fixed: the cause was AutoTextarea's measurement, not Requests
body:
Closed on 2026-07-19 when the planner's part (decompose + delegate) was done; the delegated child task b2be5889 no longer exists and the defect survived until today.

It was never specific to Requests. `AutoTextarea` measures content height by setting `height: auto`, reading `scrollHeight`, then setting the real height. For that synchronous block the element is one row tall, so the document is short by everything the textarea was; the reflow that reading `scrollHeight` forces makes the browser clamp any scroll position past the shorter maximum, and restoring the height does not restore the scroll. Measured on a task's Log, caret on the first line of a 1,700px entry: scrollY 1416 → 790 on the first keystroke, and back to 790 every time you scrolled down and typed again.

Fixed in 5bc5dd2 by carrying the scroll position across the measurement (the document's and any scrolling ancestor's), and published. Verified live: 1416 held across five keystrokes.

Unverified: the mobile half of the original report — the on-screen keyboard covering the textarea. Playwright cannot shrink the visual viewport the way a real keyboard does, so the clamp is fixed but the keyboard-overlap behaviour needs a check on a phone.

All isolated apps made available in the server; moved settings from setup-wizard into its own app.

title: Pang of mortality
body:
While waking, a pang of mortality when I recalled that I was 51 years old (almost 60). It was a sudden shock perhaps because my mind was consumed with technical systems thoughts and something about that is timeless. My mindspace is perhaps identical to that I occupied in my teens. To think of all the ways I spent my whole life, and much of it is past, and I'm still trying to solve some of the same, seemingly basic problems.

- How do I build a base that is stable. That lasts.
- How do I create a rhythm that flows.
- How do I bring order to chaos for me, my loved ones, my community, and the world.
- How do I love and receive love.

The pang was more like a great distress... that it is alost over and I've travelled so very little from where I began.

Why does nothing accrue? [@Jen](person:79ed28f0-e91e-42aa-99a2-3d50bbaab49c) stole that from me with her constant unsettledness. The base was always attacked the decisions were never solid.

To travel, we oftentimes need to destroy our bases, our mooring. Jen's fundamental mooring, to me, in her 20s, was the thing she wanted to get away from most. Ever attacking it... me. Perhaps I represented something she settled for. It wasn't fair to me or to us.

I don't even know that I care about legacy as much as I care about stability, rhythm, order, and love... but not just for myself, but for my family, loved ones, community, world. I'm a builder of community: Cross, Youth Group, [@Campus Crusade UNL](organization:aa51d45a-c9dc-41b3-8a3e-b04f25435e05), Prayer Movement, [@Orlando](location:63e333d2-873a-4f61-bc36-30e175fece18) book club, leadership at [@CCC HQ](organization:9d27fa6b-e90f-4d83-8578-f3325246b6b4), ICT, leadership at churches, [@Seattle AI Society](organization:febae1ad-aba2-4223-8bda-9cc811604631), [@CivilSociety.dev](organization:9804b2a8-e430-4f15-8a33-779d43de57f5).

Jen, literally, attached every one of these things because she, selfishly and individualistically, didn't want to give of herself beyond a point... what she called "reciprocity" was actually a desire to get away from her anxiety in relationship, her inflexibility, her demands that interaction be a certain way.

To accomplish anything worthwhile, some base, a base of your own choosing, needs to stand. There can be no compounding interest if there is no savings to begin with. Jen spent everything I saved, like a devouring locust. No matter how much money I made, she spent it. She complained and became discontent with every base I ever created for her... the ones I compromised myself on to begin with. In the end, she promised me nothing but more of the same... "I want to move to the desert", "Why aren't you ok with working for the rest of your life?", "I am moving into my hag phase of life". Her anti-capitalist, anti-colonial views weren't a critique of a system so she could build a better one; they were a continuing critique of the misery of her own internal life, grasping for ways out, proposing no solutions.

I am angry to the point of weeping. I love her and wanted to build a base with her, but I could not save her.

I feel like such a failure losing my family (my base). I must make the split from Jen worth it. I must actually build a base of my own.

---

Another, less relational, but no less real aspect of the distress above, is a feeling of how I am still, STILL, trying to put together a tech foundation that works for me, that makes me more productive, helps me accomplish the stability, rhythm, order, and yes, even love that I have tried 35 years to attain (without knowing what I was doing, granted).

I blame it on Windows. I blame it on [@Adobe](organization:6f717c27-354d-43f1-9ab7-3f7cac216ebc). On the record industry. On cronies in government. On [@Apple](organization:9d7b9f2e-7df5-46cc-8b99-30b1b28121be).

We had the Internet and Linux in the 70s. We had the web in the 90s. Between then and now, these corporations enriched themselves while making everything non-interoperable, centralized, paywalled, advertised, enshittified. Then, they began using us against each other.

This was my though waking: I need my own base. Fuck [@Microsoft](organization:4ae25353-5ebb-4725-936a-84b5eb4684e4). Fuck apps. Fuck centralized providers. The future is starting again where we went off-path: the Internet, linux. Self-hosting. Empowerment.

`box-01` is my beachhead.

Build.

---

Just received from Jen:

```txt
[@Paul](person:0b085c55-5431-4cd4-89d1-af1bf1b5e817),

I find it increasingly unpleasant to initiate contact with you, but I'm doing it for myself because it helps me to get out in front of something, which is - I'm not willing or open to sharing space with you around important upcoming kid events unless you fix things with me.

Jen
```

Contemplating:

```txt
Jen,

I've not stopped thinking about our situation since we last talked. It is very important to me that we figure out how to be in each other's lives. I haven't yet written because I've been trying to work through my anger and despair of our relationship and our marriage ending. Each time I think I am about ready, I tap into another vein that gives me pause. I've felt clear and hopeful and ready at various points, but it's slippery.

I AM working on it. I am looking for solid footing... lots of journaling, and therapy, and puzzling, and meditation. I don't want to yank you around, so I want whatever I say to be authentic and stable, and I've been working towards that. I ALSO realize that the longer I wait, the higher the risk of you just deciding you never want to hear from me again. The awareness of this keeps this on my mind almost continuously.

I reread this email you sent me in November often:

"Hey Paul, I'm wondering how our current relationship agreement is feeling to you. I'm finding it sad. Not devastating, just sad, like we have each other at an arms' length with too long of an arm. I don't want to propose any big changes, but I've wished for a little more... ease? with being in touch. There was a meme I wanted to send you the other day. I've wanted to ask about your holiday plans, out of simple curiosity as a friend I care about more than as our kids' dad. If what we're doing is really working for you, then ok, but thought I'd ask. I know we really hurt each other this past year, and we've also known each other since we were 17 year old kids. I find continuously that that ends up mattering more to me than the ways we've maneuvered, badly, the end of our marriage. Not in some dumb forgive and forget way, but maybe forgive because I really think we're both good people who just don't handle things well sometimes because we're intense and in uncharted territory. -- Jen"

I resonate... 17 year old kids, maneuvered badly, mattering, good people, intense, and uncharted.

I think about the ways our lives will still be connected... about kids events, and also the house, and the extended family, and... I care about you, that 17 year old that I spent so much life with. I don't want to hate you. I don't want to be hated. I don't want the hurt to be my primary feeling. I want peace and joy for both of us.

How are you feeling these days? What are you thinking? What does sharing space and fixing things look like for you?

P.
```

title: How I feel about support and boundaries
body:
What I want to say to [@Fiona](person:40f1bbfa-f375-4a65-84d9-1290fd02a3c7) and [@Sinead](person:72a05873-c2c7-4de6-b5e2-ae6c2abcf2d3): "How are you? How are you
really? I'm not happy with how my support for you has just become
financial, I want you to know I am available to support you in all ways.
I know that won't look like how mom supports you, we're very different
people. But I do want you to know I am here for you, with all of me. I
miss you and I'm not happy with not being more in your life."

Sort of what I want to say to [@Jen](person:79ed28f0-e91e-42aa-99a2-3d50bbaab49c):

Thank you for giving me the space to work through my anger and
resentment towards you. \[This past year shed light on ways I have had
my boundaries violated by you over and over throughout our relationship,
in ways I hadn't seen so clearly before\]. Christmas was a hard
separation, but, I think helpful for me in gaining some clarity.

Broken relationships are terrible to carry, like open wounds that keep
us from healing and moving forward. I don't want to feel that rawness
every time we interact in the future. I want our interactions with each
other and those around us to be joyful and warm. For that to happen, we
need to resolve our relationship, come to a place of gratitude for the
time we had together, find forgiveness for the hurt, and treat each
other in ways we both deserve \[boundaries\].

I care about you as someone who has shared so much life with me. I
wouldn't have done that with just anyone, you are special. I've tried to
rewrite my recording of our history together in ways that help me deal
with the pain of our divorce, internalizing you as the person who
treated me badly, but I can't find resolution this way. The fact is, I
will always cherish the time we spent together. You and I grew up
together and built a family together and impacted each other in ways
that formed the incredible people we are today.

We hurt each other so much. Ultimately, we weren't compatible as lovers,
or as sojourners and went through a chaotic time of pulling ourselves
apart from each other. I believe separation was good for both of us,
that we can be grateful for the good times, forgive each other for the
bad times, and respect one another as we continue on in different
directions. We have had loose and undefined boundaries for most of our
relationship, and especially these past few years as we've experimented
with various ways of staying connected. I do think we can do better, and
more than anything, I want to settle on something that is good for both
of us now.

We both care about our daughters more than anything in this world. I
want to continue investing in our daughters well and I want to work with
you to do that. I want your thoughts on how I can show up better. I
won't always agree with you, but I value your heart for our kids.

I don't want you to feel like preparing the house for sale is all on
you. We built that home together and I want to see it through. You can
rely on me to help fix up the remaining items for that transition.

Moving forward, I think it's best to close off connection around other
areas, to allow each other to find our personal and social connection in
our separate ways. Outside of our house and children, it's best we find
our emotional and social support elsewhere. I know this isn't black and
white.

Ultimately, I want to be in a place where our daughters feel supported,
our house is resolved, and you and I can share warmth when our paths
cross.
